title: Mini-tier anchoring - back-of-envelope
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick personal scratchpad to test a tiny hybrid: low-cost starter packs + PAYG for overage. Want something that feels "sticky" without heavy discounts.
- Use cases targeted: small dev teams, early-stage startups, prototypes that make frequent small calls (chat widgets, internal copilots).
- Constraints: keep friction low for self-serve; avoid immediate margin bleed; simple to explain on the signup page.

Assumptions (rough; refine with telemetry):
- Hosted inference marginal cost approximations (back-of-envelope):
  - Effective GPU cost per token served (amortized): $0.000008/token (8e-6). Derived from: GPU $/hr + infra + networking + infra ops. See note below.
  - Average token payload per request: 250 tokens (user+model). (Mix of short completions + chat snippets)
  - Requests per month per small team: 2.5k requests (~625k tokens) baseline.
  - Blended gross margin target for hosted: 60–70% initially for starter packs.

Starter pack idea A (small):
- Price: $20/month credit bundle. Credits: 50k tokens (translates to $0.0004/token equivalent).
- If used fully: revenue per token = $20/50k = $0.0004/token. Server cost at 8e-6/token -> cost = $0.000008 * 50k = $0.4 -> Wait miscalc, re-evaluate:
  - cost = 50,000 tokens * 0.000008 = $0.40 (yes)
  - gross margin = ($20 - $0.40) / $20 = 98% (seems high; pricing includes value capture + support + infra overhead allocations).
  - We should bucket additional fixed costs (billing, customer support, SRE): add $2 of overhead per active small account -> adjusted margin = ($20 - $0.40 - $2)/$20 = 87%
- Behavioral anchor: 50k tokens covers ~2000 requests at 250 tokens/request -> if a team makes 2.5k requests, they'd need a small top-up payg.

Starter pack idea B (very small intro):
- Price: $5/month -> credits 12k tokens (implied $0.000416/token).
- Cost for provider = 12k * 0.000008 = $0.096 -> overhead push = $1 (billing churn etc) -> margin ~ (5 - 0.096 - 1)/5 = 80%
- Use case: trialing product, low risk for us; good for driving signups.

Pay-as-you-go overage pricing suggestion:
- Keep per-token PAYG at $0.0008/token for the first year as anchor for small customers (this is 2x the starter equivalent).
- Rationale: anchor high to make starter packs look like a deal but not so high that overage kills adoption.
- Example: Customer uses 100k tokens in a month after using $20 pack (50k included):
  - Pack covers 50k -> remaining 50k charged at $0.0008 -> $40 overage -> total bill $60.
  - Effective blended rate for 100k = $60/100k = $0.0006/token.
  - Provider cost for 100k = 100k * 8e-6 = $0.80 -> huge margin in absolute terms.

Hybrid seat+token thought (quick):
- For small teams that value predictability, offer seat at $10/dev/month + 10k tokens. This gives some predictable revenue and still monetizes usage. But probably too many dimensions for simple onboarding. Keep optional.

Anchoring and conversion considerations:
- Psychological anchor: show pack X tokens (~equivalent number of chat sessions) + immediate credits on signup.
- Show compare-to-PAYG math: "Starter pack saves you Y% vs on-demand" with actual numbers.
- Offer one-click top-up buttons: +$5, +$20, +$100.

Sensible limits and anti-abuse:
- Rate cap the starter pack to prevent a single user from running long-run long-hot sessions that are cheap for them and expensive for us (e.g., long decode loops).
- Soft throttles after sustained high throughput.

Quick sensitivity checks (play with key variables):
1) If effective server cost is 3x (0.000024/token) because long sequences/low batching:
   - Cost for 50k tokens = $1.20 -> still tiny vs $20 pack. Margin after $2 overhead: (20 - 1.2 - 2)/20 = 82%
2) If median usage for a starter pack user drops to 10k tokens/month (pack waste):
   - They consume 20% of pack -> perceived value depends on retention. Need to design N months credit expiry or rollover to not encourage hoarding.

Churn/back-of-envelope LTV calc (very rough):
- Assume avg ARPU for starter cohort = $15/mo (mix of $5, $20 packs & some PAYG overage).
- Assume gross margin ~70% after overheads (conservative). -> gross contribution = $10.5/mo.
- If avg retention = 8 months -> LTV = $84.
- CAC target: aim CAC < $40 for profitable payback (2–3 month payback).
- This implies top-of-funnel cost must be tight; viral/organic channels preferred.

Operational notes / engineering constraints:
- Need cheap, atomic top-up flow in console + mobile web.
- Billing engine must allow credits balance and first-consume pack credits before PAYG. (Ticket: JIRA PR-1284)
- Rate-limits per account and per-API-key variable based on pack tier.
- Instrument metrics: tokens_used_by_pack, tokens_overage, pack_repurchase_rate, days_to_topup.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm real marginal token cost from infra (SRE/infra: velocity.env cost model) — ask Ravi.
- Experiment idea: A/B test $20 pack vs $15 pack + higher PAYG (which increases anchoring).
- Decide expiry model: 90-day expiry? monthly rollover? (Pros/cons: retention vs hoarding).
- Explore low-cost per-seat add-on for teams that want admin controls.

Slack / refs:
- See slack thread #pricing-ops 3/nov/25 (summary pinned).
- Confluence: PRICING-ANCHORS-2025 for earlier cohort analysis and historical pack performance.
- Related ticket: JIRA PR-1284 (billing credits implementation).

Final quick recommendation (for next discussion):
- Ship 2 starter offers: $5/12k tokens and $20/50k tokens + PAYG at $0.0008/token.
- No rollover for initial launch; test 90-day expiry for $5 pack, 180-day for $20 pack.
- Add top-up CTAs in console and email triggers at 20% remaining.
- Instrument remaining metrics and run 8-week A/B test to measure repurchase and conversion-to-paid.

Notes to self: keep messaging simple. Avoid too many toggles in UI at launch.

Quick scratch math summary (clean numbers):
- Provider marginal cost assumption: $0.000008/token.
- $5 pack: 12k tokens -> provider cost $0.096 -> overhead $1 -> margin ~80%
- $20 pack: 50k tokens -> provider cost $0.40 -> overhead $2 -> margin ~87%
- PAYG anchor: $0.0008/token (100x provider marginal cost) -> makes packs feel like a deal but still profitable.

-- end scratchpad --
